title: Present tense: regular -are verbs
rule: Stem + -o, -i, -a, -iamo, -ate, -ano. Spelling keeps the sound: -care/-gare add h before i; -ciare/-giare/-iare drop the stem's i before i. Stress stays on the stem in the loro form.

head: Group
Verbs
What happens
Example
rows: parlare, lavorare, abitare, aspettare, comprare, guardare, ascoltare, ordinare, arrivare, entrare, tornare
h before the endings in -i and -iamo
the stem's i merges with the ending's i

items.n: I work at the bar. / I'm working at the bar.

items.note: near future, with a time word

items.n: I've been living here for a month.
items.note: present + da for "have been doing": unit 8

items.n: Do you speak English? — Yes, I do.
items.note: no "do"; the verb repeats in the answer

blocks.title: Stress in the loro form
blocks.text: [[PARlano]], [[LAvorano]], [[ORdinano]], [[TElefonano]]: the stress is where it is in the io form. Saying parLAno is the single most common pronunciation error in this tense, and Italians hear it instantly.

items.why: No auxiliary "am"; the simple present does it.
H to keep the hard sound.

items.wrong: Ascolto a la radio. Guardo a la TV.
items.right: Ascolto la radio. Guardo la TV.

items.q: Dora e Nando ___ (parlare) in dialetto; io ___ (ascoltare) e non ___ (capire)… quasi.
items.n: Dora and Nando speak dialect; I listen and don't understand… almost.
